Digital Health Humanities Toolkit

The Digital Health Humanities Toolkit is a website containing the lesson plans developed for the Advancing Digital Health Humanities Institute (ADHHI).

This site is a repository of lessons developed during the ADHHI's two-year program. They are designed to onboard learners to the basics of digital humanities research, from the use of specific tools and workflows, to the problems and ethical considerations that guide digital health research.

The ADHHI was a National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH)-funded research incubator that supported computational research into the human experiences of health and illness. It ran from April 2024 to June 2026.

Read the White Paper

Digital Humanities Crash Course

What are the Digital Humanities?

This introduction outlines the digital humanities that this lesson, and the toolkit more broadly, frames

  1. Students will learn the basic tensions which guide digital humanities scholarship.
  2. Students will learn how social constructivism informs humanities approaches to data.
  3. Students will develop an understanding of how data is used by digital technologies and programs.

Understanding Digital Research: A Hands-On Lesson

This lesson will teach learners about different digital methods and how they fit into humanistic research.

  1. Students will learn about how digital methods can be incorporated into humanities research
  2. Students will engage with historical data to understand how data is structured in material documents
  3. Students will learn about how to choose a specific method based on their research interests.

Applying Digital Methods to Your Research

This lesson will teach learners about different digital methods and how they fit into humanistic research.

  1. Students will learn about different digital methods
  2. Students will understand how those methods link into digital humanities research
  3. Students will learn how to think about their projects from a position that incorporates computational methods.
